nicknames: Home of the Albury Gold Cup

main_turf.bias_notes: Clockwise. A spacious, championship-standard 2,100m country oval with broad sweeping turns and a generous 400m home straight. The wide layout and long run-in make it one of the fairest galloping surfaces in regional NSW, giving mid-pack stalkers ('P') and closing swoopers ('S') a genuine chance to wind up.
main_turf.post_bias: Barrier draws are generally fair across most route starts. In 1000m and 1175m sprint starts, inside-to-middle barriers (2-6) are slightly preferred to ensure a smooth position before entering the home bend.

handicapping_angles.border_form_cross_over: Albury sits directly on the NSW/VIC border. Always cross-reference Victorian country form (Wodonga, Wangaratta, Benalla, Bendigo) against local NSW form. Victorian country shippers dropping into NSW country benchmark company carry a proven class edge.
handicapping_angles.albury_cup_class_spike: During the autumn Albury Gold Cup Carnival (1500m / 2000m Listed), major Sydney and Melbourne metropolitan stables (Maher, Waterhouse/Bott, Waller) send high-class pattern horses to the border. Heavily upgrade metropolitan shippers over local regional runners.
handicapping_angles.fair_400m_straight_swooper_upgrade: Albury's broad turns and 400m home straight prevent front-runners from locking up the race. Do not hesitate to back strong-finishing closers with high L400m speed ratings.
handicapping_angles.nsw_country_benchmark_weight_penalty: In NSW Country Benchmark races (BM58-BM74), top weights carrying 60kg+ face a strict penalty over the 400m straight (1kg = ~1 length). In Listed feature events (Albury Cup), ignore minor weight spreads and prioritize peak class and rated form.
